title: Opening grammar
description: Which kind of opening belongs between which two rooms. One file, openings/grammar.json, checked by build/check_openings.py. Every rule is editorial by ruling (26 Aug 2026) and must quote the corpus prose it reads — a rule with no basis is a guess, and a guess with a band on it is the laundering this corpus exists to prevent.

kind.description: There is no other value. The day a rule here is sourced, this becomes an enum and that rule says which source.

note.description: The file's own honesty note. Long on purpose: it has to say what was read, what was fitted, and what may not be promoted without the blocked facsimiles.

side.description: One end of an opening. `any` matches anything; `type` is a room-catalogue id or the literal 'exterior'; `function_class` is one or several.

when.description: Unordered: a door between two rooms is one door and matches either way round. Absent only on the default rule, which matches everything left.

type.description: Same enum as the plan schema's door.type — the grammar may not invent a kind of opening the record cannot hold.

derive_width_from.description: Where a proportion pack states this width, the pack wins and the band only clamps it. The corpus deriving its own dimension is always better than a band fitted here.

basis.description: The corpus prose this rule reads, quoted verbatim with its record named. Not optional and not a paraphrase: an editorial call whose basis cannot be checked against the record it claims to read is indistinguishable from an invention.
